subject: Urgent: Wavefront latency storm — temporary reroute & escalation
messages:
From: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@wavefront.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 21:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike in US-WEST2 (urgent)

Jonas —

We started seeing a pretty large latency and 5xx spike at ~20:30 PST affecting ~45% of our production inference traffic (US-WEST2). Latency p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s and we're seeing a burst of 502/504 errors. This is impacting customer-facing features.

We attached a CSV with the sample error bursts and a screenshot of our SLO dashboard. Can Redwood route our production traffic off us-west2 while you investigate? Our product team would prefer us-east (us-east1) or us-east2 as an alternative.

We need an ETA for mitigation and a point of contact for exec updates. If possible, we'd like temporary credits for the degraded window.

Regards,
Amelia Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops, Wavefront Inc.
attachments: wavefront-error-log-20280118.csv, slo-dashboard-screenshot.png
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@wavefront.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 21:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike in US-WEST2 (urgent)

Amelia — thanks for the heads up and for the files. We've seen a correlated spike in platform telemetry. I'm escalating to SRE and CS.

Immediate plan (short):
- Put you in a temporary routing policy to prefer us-east1 while we investigate (requires SRE go-ahead).
- SRE to run a K/V cache sanity and model-variant fallback to reduce compute pressure.
- I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes; Sean will join if leadership coordination is needed.

Marissa / Soojin: can you confirm we have capacity in us-east1 (or us-east2) for a short-term soft-redirect? If we do the redirect, estimate for full traffic rehome and burn-rate impact?

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415 555 0198
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sear_chad@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 21:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike in US-WEST2 (urgent)

Jonas / Marissa —

We see a spike in backpressure on the us-west2 GPU pool starting 2028-01-18T20:28:00 PST. Root symptoms: elevated token-queue length on a small set of long-sequence requests (customer QPS profile shifted) + transient degraded kernel scheduling on two nodes (likely host-level OOM early signs). 5xxs originate from model worker restarts and overloaded dispatchers.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Soft-redirect (HTTP 307) new sessions to us-east1 with in-flight sticky sessions allowed to drain — low risk and fastest.
2) Activate model-variant with 8-bit quantization for the affected customer to lower per-token compute — reduces quality slightly but cuts load ~30%.
3) Add ephemeral burst capacity to us-west2 (if infra has spare GPUs available) — takes ~18-30 minutes to provision.

I recommend option 1 + option 2 as combined — do route-pref to us-east1 and enable quantized variant for Wavefront. Need Marissa or Jonas to confirm customer consent for quality tradeoff (Amelia already asked for re-route).

I'll prepare the routing change and a runbook snippet; will need Sean or Markus for approval on unilateral credits if the incident goes beyond 30 minutes.

— Soojin Lee
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@wavefront.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 21:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike in US-WEST2 (urgent)

Amelia — appreciate the prompt report. Jonas and Soojin outlined the mitigation steps. We're ready to execute a soft-redirect to us-east1 and to enable the quantized variant. Two asks before we proceed:

1) Can you confirm Wavefront is okay with a temporary model-variant (8-bit) for a short window? We expect a small delta in output fidelity for some prompts.
2) Please confirm the requested rehome window and whether you'd prefer us-east1 or us-east2 (us-east1 has slightly lower current utilization).

If you confirm, we'll start the routing change now and monitor closely. We'll also draft a credit proposal for inhale-time SLA degradation and loop Legal/Finance.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Amelia Ruiz

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike in US-WEST2 (incident follow-up & exec note)

Team — thanks for the quick action. Per Soojin and Jonas the soft-redirect + quantized-variant was applied at 21:54 PST and Wavefront traffic completed warm-up into us-east1 by ~22:12 PST. Error rates dropped to baseline and p95 latency returned to ~140ms.

Next steps (for internal runbook and exec):
- Soojin: complete post-mortem and include host-level kernel scheduling note + mitigation checklist.
- Marissa: send Wavefront the proposed credit terms and a one-page incident summary for their execs. Use DEAL-8741 for reference.
- Markus: loop Legal on the credit term in the attached PDF and approve up to 5% one-time credit if the post-mortem shows platform-side root cause.

I'll draft a short exec update for our COO and will flag if we need broader communication. Good work everyone.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
